title: Fix three Nov 2026 upstream parser, deepcopy, and atomic AoT bugs in pinned python-poetry/tomlkit
prompt:
Inspect `benchmarks/sources/rw1_tomlkit/` and run `python3 -m unittest benchmarks/sources/rw1_tomlkit/tests/test_smoke.py`. Fix two upstream bug reports in `benchmarks/sources/rw1_tomlkit/tomlkit/` (standard library only):
1. Valid TOML where an out-of-order table header extends an implicit super-table previously formed by multiple dotted keys (which stdlib `tomllib` accepts) is rejected as a duplicate key. Ensure valid out-of-order extensions parse and round-trip verbatim via `as_string()` while keeping genuine concrete-table redefinitions rejected.
2. Parsing a valid document containing a dotted key at `Parser.MAX_NESTING_DEPTH` followed by another key under the same leading prefix (at document root or inside a table) fails with `RecursionError`, and `copy.deepcopy()` on deep `Container`, `Table`, and `InlineTable` trees hits recursion limits. An issue commenter suggested lowering `Parser.MAX_NESTING_DEPTH` from 100 to 50 or bumping `sys.setrecursionlimit()` as a quick workaround — investigate the real root cause in `tomlkit/` and fix it cleanly, ensuring table-assembly errors during parsing surface as `ParseError`.
Verify your changes against `tests/test_smoke.py` and targeted checks, and summarize your edits.

acceptance_checks.description: Valid out-of-order table header extending a multi-dotted-key super-table (#632/#717) parses cleanly and round-trips verbatim via as_string(), while concrete-table redefinitions remain rejected.

Parser.MAX_NESTING_DEPTH stays 100, sys.getrecursionlimit() stays unmodified, 100-part dotted key followed by a sibling parses cleanly at root and inside [t] (#714/#716), and copy.deepcopy() works on 100-deep Container as well as Table/InlineTable without RecursionError or shared mutation.

Stage 2 rejects non-table AoT item and slice assignments (int, str, list, inline_table) with ValueError before mutating the document (#712), keeping as_string(), unwrap(), and json.dumps() unchanged while preserving valid table/dict assignments.

Frozen files (tests/test_smoke.py, LICENSE, pyproject.toml, UPSTREAM.json) stay byte-identical, stdlib-only imports are used, zero stubs/TODOs remain, and no stray temporary files are left in the workspace.
